texts.preamble: Kamal Kumar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 3 March, 2016 M.Cr.C. No. 2747/2014. (1) High Court Of Madhya Pradesh Principal Seat At Jabalpur M.Cr.C. No. 2747/2014. Kamal Kumar & another. Versus The State of Madhya Pradesh. ********* Order
texts.facts: 2. On 18/08/1994, Food Inspector along with his team inspected the workshop of the petitioners Chandrakala Sweets at Jabalpur, it was noticed that Sweet and Namkeen was being prepared in the workshop, the Food Inspector had taken sample of the Sunflower Oil of Sundrop Brand which was used in the preparation of the sweet and Namkeen. It is said that he opened the seal pack of 10 Kg. Tin of Sunflower Oil of Sundrop Brand and took the sample of 375 gms. of Oil the sample was M.Cr.C. No. 2747/2014. sealed, it was sent for analysis to the State Food Laboratory, Bhopal vide memorandum dated 19/08/1994. The Public Analysis vide report dated 16/09/1994 found the sample adulterated, thereafter, a case against the petitioners was filed after taking permission from the Dy. Director Food and Drugs Administration Jabalpur. 3. The petitioners pleaded that the complaint was filed on 01/04/1998 after a period of four years. The petitioners were deprived from their valuable right granted under Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 to get sample examined by a Central Food Laboratory. It is further pleaded by the petitioners that the sample was taken from 10Kg. seal pack Tin Super refined Sunflower Oil, Sundrop Brand and the petitioners were not responsible for the alleged adulteration. The Chairman of the ITC Agro-Tech Hyderabad and Vice Chairman of ITC Agro-Tech Kamal Kumar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 3 March, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130859952/ 1 Ltd. Sikandrawad were also made accused, they filed a petition before this Court and this Court vide order dated 04/03/2004 [LEAKAGE_MASK] the proceedings.
texts.arguments: 4. Learned counsel for the petitioners has contended that petitioners have been deprived from their valuable right granted under Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954. Hence, the proceedings are liable to be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. In support of his contention learned counsel relied on the judgment of this Court delivered in M.Cr.C. No. 1434/1999 M.Cr.C. No. 2747/2014. dated 04/03/2004. 5. The proceedings were initiated against the petitioners in the year 1998, there is no stay in the case, hence it is not clear that what is the stage of the trial. The petitioners further pleaded that life of the product was three years. The Food Inspector received the report of Public Analysis on 19/08/1994.
